q: Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity K^t(x) (Ct-complexity) restricts to programs running in ≤ t(|x|) steps. Its relationship to circuit complexity is:
opts: K^t(x) = circuit complexity of x always
K^t(x) ≈ the size of the smallest circuit computing x in the given time bound (up to logarithmic factors)
K^t(x) is always greater than K(x)
K^t(x) is computable for any t
exp: Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity is closely related to circuit complexity: K^{poly}(x) ≈ the minimum circuit size computing x (Sipser, Schnorr). This connection links descriptional complexity to computational complexity, and is related to the P vs NP question.
